current_status.from: Extended and active as of 2026-08-19. Imperial County's Board extended the initial 45-day emergency pause to a one-year moratorium while the Data Center Advisory Committee evaluates zoning and land-use policy; reporting describes the pause as running into June 2027.
current_status.to: Rescinded by court order as of 2026-09-23. Imperial County Superior Court Judge Jeffrey B. Jones entered judgment 2026-09-04 in favor of developer Imperial Valley Computer Manufacturing, LLC, finding neither Ordinance 1616 (the original moratorium) nor Ordinance 1618 (its ~10-month-15-day extension) made the causal finding of a 'current and immediate threat to public health, safety, or welfare' required by Gov. Code section 65858. A peremptory writ of mandate issued 2026-09-11 directs the County and Board of Supervisors to set aside both ordinances and stop using them to withhold, suspend, or refuse data-center permits. The County has said (per KYMA, 2026-09-22) it is working on a new moratorium addressing the court's concerns; no replacement had been adopted as of 2026-09-23. The Data Center Advisory Committee, created alongside the moratorium, continues to meet (inaugural meeting 2026-09-17) and is unaffected by the ruling. Separately, a different judge (L. Brooks Anderholt) has ordered a full CEQA environmental review of the underlying data center project in a related case, so the project itself remains stalled notwithstanding the moratorium's invalidation.

new_candidates.duration: Interim administrative prohibition on processing/approving large-scale (hyperscale) AI data centers in unincorporated county zones, in effect until the Board of Supervisors adopts a permanent zoning ordinance. A motion to formally initiate that ordinance was scheduled for a Community Services Cluster Agenda Review on 2026-09-23, with a Board of Supervisors hearing expected around 2026-10-06.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Department of Regional Planning Director's memorandum (interim planning guidance), issued pursuant to and implementing the Board of Supervisors' unanimous April 14, 2026 motion (Solis) directing staff to study and recommend data-center zoning code amendments; a formal ordinance was in preparation as of this pass, not yet adopted by the Board.
new_candidates.trigger: San Gabriel Valley community concerns over health, environmental, water, and electricity impacts of hyperscale AI data centers (following the Monterey Park/SDCF controversy and other regional moratoria); Board of Supervisors motion directing a zoning study; noise, air-quality, and utility-rate concerns cited by county Public Health and Public Works directors.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23. On Sept. 17, 2026, LA County's Department of Regional Planning director issued a memorandum imposing an immediate, interim prohibition on new hyperscale AI data center development in all zones of unincorporated county territory (about 1 million of the county's 10 million residents), pending Board of Supervisors adoption of a formal ordinance. A motion to formally initiate that ordinance was on the agenda for a Sept. 23, 2026 Community Services Cluster Agenda Review meeting, with Board consideration expected around Oct. 6, 2026. Smaller enterprise/accessory/sole-source data centers are not covered by the prohibition.
new_candidates.affected_projects: No hyperscale data centers currently sited in unincorporated county areas as of the memo; about 74 data centers operate elsewhere within LA County (mostly in incorporated cities), unaffected by the county action.
new_candidates.outcome: Interim administrative ban imposed via Regional Planning Director memorandum while the Board of Supervisors moves to adopt a permanent zoning ordinance banning hyperscale AI data centers in unincorporated areas.
